subject: A/B rollout SLA safeguard proposal for BrightFin — auto-fallback & pinning
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@brightfin.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ops@brightfin.com
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: SLA impact during our upcoming A/B rollout

Hi Chloe,

Quick note ahead of our scheduled A/B on Friday — our legal/SRE team flagged risk of transient latency spikes during your canary causing a breach of our 99.95% latency SLA. We rely on tight tail-latency guarantees for production fraud detection, and even short blips can cascade.

Can you share the contingency you plan to use if the canary produces a latency/EER (error/event-rate) spike? Specifically: automatic fallback behavior, whether you can pin the previous stable model/version for affected traffic, and how long the pin would hold before manual intervention. We also need instrumentation evidence (telemetry hooks) to validate the failover when it happens.

We need this by EOD today so our legal team can sign off the short SLO addendum.

Thanks,
Marta
Marta Lopez
SRE Manager, BrightFin

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: SLA impact during our upcoming A/B rollout

Team — forwarding BrightFin's ask. TL;DR: they want an explicit auto-fallback + version pin for canary failures and evidence for SRE/legal.

Proposal (first pass):
- Canary scope: 2% traffic for 60 minutes (can shorten if BrightFin requests).
- Auto-fallback trigger: sustained 2-minute rolling average latency > 1.5x baseline OR error-rate spike > 3x baseline for 90s.
- Auto-action: immediate traffic swap back to pinned stable version; pinned version remains locked for 10 minutes after auto-fallback. Manual override required to unpin earlier.
- Warmup: aggressive KV cache pre-warm for the model path; prefetch top-100 prefixes before canary begins.
- Telemetry: expose a dedicated SLO dashboard and a webhook for BrightFin ops when auto-fallback fires. We'll include a short event payload schema.

Attachments: brightfin_canary_escape_plan_v1.pdf (detailed thresholds, rollback playbook, and telemetry payload).

Ask: Karthik, can you confirm runtime-level feasibility (kernel selection, cache warmup) and whether we can make the auto-unpin require an explicit API call? Laura/Sean, please confirm SRE alignment on the webhook + runbook. I want to send this to Marta with an estimated timeline by EOD.

-Chloe
Chloe Martin
Senior Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 10:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: SLA impact during our upcoming A/B rollout

Chloe — looks good. Quick notes from runtime side:
- Auto-unpin as an explicit API call is straightforward; we'll gate it on a signed request from BrightFin ops or a Redwood SRE key.
- Recommend autorevert grace: if we see severe degradation (>=2x latency or >5% absolute error rate), perform immediate swap and keep the pin for 60 seconds before attempting a silent probe. If the probe fails, keep pinned and escalate. The 10-minute lock is OK as a post-mortem window but 60s immediate hold reduces flip-flop risk.
- We'll add a KV-cache warmup stage that preloads common prefixes and a brief traffic ramp (0% -> 0.5% -> 2% across 5 minutes) to reduce tail spikes.
- Instrumentation: we'll emit canary_event.auto_fallback and canary_event.probe_result to the SLO dashboard; we can also post a DocuSign addendum link back to BrightFin automatically when they approve the addendum.

I'll attach a one-line doc with the Docusign link for legal to sign: s3://redwood-sec/brightfin/slo-addendum-docusign-link.txt

-Karthik
Principal Infra Eng, Redwood Inference

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@brightfin.com>
Cc: ops@brightfin.com, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 14:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: SLA impact during our upcoming A/B rollout

Hi Marta — thanks for the flag and patience while we scoped this. Attached is our operational safeguard proposal for the Friday A/B (brightfin_canary_escape_plan_v1.pdf). Summary below: 

1) Canary configuration:
  - 2% traffic, staged ramp over 5 minutes (0% -> 0.5% -> 2%).
  - Duration: nominally 60 minutes; can be shortened on your request.

2) Auto-fallback triggers and actions:
  - Trigger thresholds: 2-minute rolling average latency > 1.5x baseline OR error-rate > 3x baseline for 90s. Severe condition: >=2x latency or >5% absolute error rate triggers immediate swap.
  - Action: automatic traffic reroute to the pinned stable version. Pinned version stays locked for 10 minutes after an auto-fallback. For severe conditions (immediate swap), we'll keep a 60s probe hold before any automated probe attempts; human SRE approval required to unpin earlier.

3) Runtime mitigations:
  - KV cache warmup and prefetch of top prefixes; kernel selection optimized for p95 tail workloads.
  - Silent probe behavior: after the hold window a single low-volume probe is sent; only if probe latency/error metrics are back to baseline do we allow a controlled re-introduction.

4) Observability & evidence:
  - Dedicated SLO dashboard and webhook event: canary_event.auto_fallback with payload including reason, timestamps, and request ids.
  - We will push a signed DocuSign link for the SLO addendum once you confirm acceptance.

Next steps / ask from BrightFin: please reply with "APPROVE" to this thread if you accept the above (we'll push the DocuSign link immediately). If you want tighter thresholds or a shorter canary window, let us know and we can iterate.

Thanks,
Chloe
Chloe Martin
Senior Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
